Welcome to the St Philip's School
Welcome to our website, I hope it gives you a taste of the exciting curriculum we have on offer here at St Philip’s.
I am very proud to be the Headteacher of St Philip’s School and to work with such a dedicated staff team and enthusiastic students. Our facilities are fantastic and support us to create a learning environment that helps all of our students achieve their full potential, both socially and academically. We pride ourselves on our ability to support students to become as independent as possible in all areas of their lives.
Through hard work and perseverance, all of our students progress to meaningful outcomes. Thank you for visiting the St Philip’s website and do get in touch if you require any further information.
Safeguarding Statement from the Headteacher
At St Philip’s School, the safety and well-being of every student is our highest priority. We are committed to creating a secure, supportive, and inclusive environment where all students, who have Education, Health and Care Plans, can thrive and reach their full potential.
Safeguarding is at the heart of everything we do. We adhere strictly to the statutory guidance set out in Keeping Children Safe in Education 2025 and the OFSTED inspection framework. Our safeguarding policies and procedures are robust, regularly reviewed, and fully embedded across the school community. All staff receive ongoing training to ensure they are vigilant and equipped to identify and respond to any concerns promptly and effectively.
We recognise the unique needs of our diverse student body, including those with medical conditions, English as an additional language, and those eligible for Pupil Premium funding. We work closely with families, local authorities, and multi-agency partners to safeguard and promote the welfare of our students.
Our commitment extends beyond the school gates to ensure students feel safe, respected, and valued in all areas of their lives. We encourage independence, social responsibility, and mutual respect, fostering a community where everyone’s voice is heard and protected.
Should you have any concerns about a student’s safety or well-being, please do not hesitate to contact the school’s Designated Safeguarding Lead. Together, we can ensure that St Philip’s remains a safe and nurturing place for all.
Ben Walsh – Headteacher

Ethos and Values
St Philip’s is a school where individuals are valued for themselves and where all are expected to give of their best.
School values and ethos
We believe that young people learn and develop best with clear and consistent work and behaviour expectations and where praise, enjoyment, consideration and respect are integral to the school’s life and ethos.
We encourage students to become as independent as possible in all areas of their lives, both in and out of the classroom. We challenge students to try new things, such as developing new friendships or using public transport.
The school aims to inspire curiosity, a spirit of collaboration, and develop creative thinking, a sense of social responsibility and leadership skills. A strong sense of community underpins everything we do – learning to respect each other’s backgrounds and beliefs. We value commitment, we celebrate success and we offer an environment which not only leads to academic success but also to self-discovery and a sense of personal worth and well-being.

Doing the right thing, in the right way, for the right reasons.
At OHCAT, governance is not just a statutory duty – it’s a vital part of how we lead with integrity, collaborate effectively, and make a meaningful impact. Our governors play a key role in ensuring our schools are safe, inclusive, and thriving environments for pupils and staff.

Animal Care
Animals play an important role in school life at St Philip’s. As well as the our therapy dog there are also a number of animals in school for pupils to interact with. In one Year 7 classroom, pupils can take time out from their lessons to watch or pet Aslan the rabbit or Timmy the tortoise. Pupils say it is soothing to have the animals in class with them.
We have a dedicated animal care classroom and area outside for goats to graze freely during the school day.
In Key Stage 4 students have the option to follow a course in Animal Care. The course explores animal care industries and jobs working with animals. Pupils learn how to care for different animals and the sort of hazards that could arise.
There are a number of reptiles at St Philip’s including a milk snake, a variety of geckos, a turtle, Bearded Dragon and one section of the course teaches young people how to look after these animals in a safe manner. They can also practice their skills on guinea pigs, rabbits and chickens which are kept outside in a fox-safe enclosure. Pupils enjoy stroking the soft fur and feathers, when they can catch them, and also learn how to feed and look after these animals.
All pupils on the course have to prepare a presentation to give to Primary aged children about caring for an animal of their choice. Animal Care is a popular Key Stage option which gives pupils the experience of looking after animals. Every year some of our students choose to complete an Animal Care course at local colleges.
The animals at St Philip’s are not only for education and are a valuable part of the pastoral care that we offer.

Religious Education
The RE curriculum at St Philips has been designed to fit The Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames agreed Syllabus for RE.
The RE syllabus enables pupils to know about and understand Christianity as a living faith that influences the lives of people worldwide and as the religion that has most shaped British culture and heritage. It also enables pupils to know and understand about other major world religions and world views, their impact on society, culture and the wider world, enabling pupils to express ideas and insights. Finally, it contributes to the development of pupils’ own spiritual/philosophical convictions, exploring and enriching their own beliefs and values.
The RE curriculum at St Philip’s operates under the agreed Syllabus of Kingston and covers all the necessary topics. The RE curriculum has been certified by Insight Kingston.
The Key Stage 2 and Key Stage 3 schemes of work consider how and where they can promote British values through the topics which pupil’s study. The learning intents have been designed to ensure that students reach appropriate levels at the end of Key Stage 3.
In Key Stage 4 and Key Stage 5 students further develop their religious education through the Citizenship and PSHE curriculums where they not only explore religious beliefs but also engage in ethical and philosophical discussions.
All students at St Philip’s enjoy an annual cultural celebration day in the Summer term and this provides an opportunity for them to celebrate the things they have learnt through the RE, Citizenship and PSHE lessons.
St Philip’s pupils live in a multicultural society, and they need to know all about the main 6 religions to respect the customs of the people they live with. What is more, the knowledge they acquire in KS3 will help them follow the subject of Humanities in KS4.
The rest of the topics like justice and freedom or humanism are necessary for them in their daily life. They familiarise themselves with concepts that will prepare them to lead a life as global citizens in the 21st Century.
Notification to Parents and Carers Regarding Religious Education (RE)
We would like to remind all parents and carers that they have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE) lessons, should they wish to do so. This right applies to RE lessons delivered as part of the school curriculum.
Parents who wish to withdraw their children from RE should be aware of its aims and what is covered in the RE curriculum and that they are given the opportunity to discuss this if they wish. It should be made clear whether the withdrawal is from the whole RE curriculum or specific parts of it.
If you are considering withdrawing your child, we kindly ask that you contact the school in advance to discuss your decision. This ensures that we can understand your concerns and arrange appropriate alternative provision for your child during these lessons.
Please feel free to reach out to Mr Ben Walsh (Principal) at 02083972672 if you have any questions or require further information regarding this matter.
Important – limitations to withdraw
If pupils are withdrawn from RE, schools have a duty to supervise them, though not to provide additional teaching. A pupil may be required to work in another area of the school, such as the library or break out area.
Whilst parents or carers have a right to withdraw children from RE, they should note that children may also encounter religions and beliefs and wider aspects of faith in other areas of the curriculum from which there is no right of withdrawal.
On occasion, spontaneous questions about religious matters are raised by pupils or issues related to religion arise in other curriculum subjects such as history or citizenship (PSHE). For example, schools promote community cohesion and help pupils to understand ideas about identity and diversity, feelings and emotions within both religious and non-religious contexts.

We were delighted to celebrate the achievements of all those learners who are leaving St Philip’s this summer, many of whom joined the school in Primary or Year 7.
Mr Walsh welcomed parents, carers, staff and learners to the Leavers Presentation Evening and thanked everyone for coming. Speaking to the leavers he said, “It has been an amazing journey from your first day to where you are now.”
Leavers had chosen a member of staff to act as their sponsor for the event. Their sponsors paid tribute to each individual Year 11 and Post-16 learner about their time in school and there was much laughter over photos, recollection of funny moments and a few tears were shed too.
They were recognised for their academic achievement, sporting abilities, artistic and creative talents and the friendship and kindness they showed to each other. Ambitions for the future included going on to college to study Art, Science, Animal Care, Design Technology and sport.
The learners were then presented with a Leavers’ book and hoodie and had the opportunity to have a photo taken in the celebratory balloon arch. After the formalities our visiting family and friends were invited to view the GCSE art exhibition. They were then politely asked to leave for a few hours so that the leavers could let their hair down and dance with friends at their Prom event in the marquee on the school field.
It was a truly wonderful evening celebrating the journey and achievements of our 2026 leavers.
Good luck to you all – St Philip’s will miss you!
